channel.title: Crypto Front Page
channel.description: Crypto Front Page reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto industry.

item.title: Where ERC-20 and NFT Token Approvals Are Stored
item.description: Where are token approvals stored? ERC-20 allowances live in token contracts, while NFT approvals live in collection contracts, where transfer permissions are checked.

item.title: How to check a Bitcoin bridge’s collateralization before using it
item.description: Learn how to check a Bitcoin bridge’s collateralization by matching each Locker’s collateral to its obligations, then compare the ratio with any published threshold.

item.title: A First Crypto Bridge Transfer, Step by Step
item.description: What to tell a friend before their first crypto bridge transfer: explain the two chains and gas tokens, normal waits, explorer checks, and why seed phrases stay private.

item.title: Should I use hardware for regular SyncSwap swaps?
item.description: Hardware wallet vs separate hot wallet for DeFi swaps: use hardware for balances you cannot afford to lose, or cap a separately seeded hot wallet for routine trades.

item.title: Ethereum-to-Sui bridge transfer states: an evidence model
item.description: Represent Ethereum-to-Sui bridge transfer states from receipts, bridge records and Sui execution; keep RPC freshness separate so recovery stays clear.

item.title: US court orders target $1.2 billion from Binance hack
item.description: The Justice Department says court orders now cover more than $1.2 billion of Binance hack proceeds, as investigators and crypto firms trace and freeze funds.

item.title: Risks of restaking ETH compared to regular staking: what changes
item.description: Risks of restaking ETH compared to regular staking include extra AVS slashing, contract and operator risks, and a longer exit; here is what to watch.

item.title: TeleSwap locker risk vs smart contract risk: what to manage first
item.description: TeleSwap locker risk vs smart contract risk: contract bugs usually reach more holders, while collateral limits one Locker failure. Learn what to manage first.

item.title: How to Restake stETH With a Hardware Wallet
item.description: To set up a hardware wallet to restake ETH, connect Ledger or Trezor through MetaMask or Rabby, then approve, deposit and delegate an LST on-device.

item.title: What does a slippage error mean on a TRON DEX swap?
item.description: A slippage tolerance exceeded error on a TRON DEX means the swap's output fell below your minimum; refresh the quote and adjust tolerance only as needed.

item.title: DOJ gets authority over $1.2 billion in Binance theft funds
item.description: The Justice Department says it won court authority over more than $1.2 billion of Binance theft funds, advancing recovery while laundering efforts continue.

item.title: Biggest crypto bridge hacks show how one flaw can drain a vault
item.description: The biggest crypto bridge hacks came from stolen keys and flawed message checks; one approval failure could drain a vault and leave wrapped tokens unbacked.

item.title: What Is Block Finality? Why Your Bridge Transfer Waits
item.description: Block finality is when a block can no longer be reversed. Bridges wait so a deposit cannot vanish after its funds are released on another chain.

item.title: How to restake an LST and delegate it on EigenLayer
item.description: First time restaking on EigenLayer: fund a wallet, deposit a supported LST, delegate it to an operator, and verify the balance on Ethereum.

item.title: USDC from Polygon to Ethereum: Aggregator Routes
item.description: How to move USDC from Polygon to Ethereum: keep POL for gas, choose the USDC you hold, then approve and confirm a route to Ethereum mainnet.

item.title: Shibarium’s Checkpointed Sidechain Design
item.description: Is Shibarium a layer 2 or a sidechain? It is a checkpointed sidechain: BONE-staked validators confirm transactions, while Ethereum records checkpoints.

item.title: DOJ gets authority over $1.2 billion in Binance hack funds
item.description: The Justice Department says courts authorized seizure or restraint of more than $1.2 billion in Binance hack funds, part of $2.7 billion frozen overall.

item.title: How to Check a ShibaSwap Trade on Etherscan
item.description: To check an Ethereum swap transaction on Etherscan, search its wallet hash, read the status, then compare token transfers with the trade you intended.

item.title: US authorizes seizure of $1.2 billion in Binance hack funds
item.description: The Justice Department has court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of Binance hack funds, part of a wider freeze still being traced.

item.title: Difference between RenBridge and RenVM: app versus network
item.description: RenBridge was the web app for requesting cross-chain transfers; RenVM was the Darknode network that held the underlying assets and signed the messages…
